🐛 Describe the bug
Calling the C++ API torch::nn::MultiheadAttention with crafted options triggers a division-by-zero in MultiheadAttentionImpl::reset().
Reproducer
#include <torch/torch.h>

int main() {
  torch::set_num_threads(1);
  torch::Tensor query = torch::randint(1, {1, 1}, torch::TensorOptions().dtype(torch::kBool));

  auto key =
      at::quantize_per_tensor(
          torch::randn({1, 1, 1},
                       torch::TensorOptions().dtype(torch::kFloat32)),
          0.1,
          10,
          c10::kQUInt2x4);

  auto value =
      torch::randint(
          (1 << 15) - 1,
          {},
          torch::TensorOptions().dtype(torch::kInt64));

  auto key_padding_mask =
      torch::randint(
          (1 << 15) - 1,
          {1, 1, 1},
          torch::TensorOptions().dtype(torch::kInt64));

  auto attn_mask =
      torch::randn(
          {},
          torch::TensorOptions().dtype(torch::kFloat32));

  auto options =
      torch::nn::MultiheadAttentionOptions(0, 0)
          .dropout(20.0)
          .bias(true)
          .add_bias_kv(true)
          .add_zero_attn(false)
          .kdim(0)
          .vdim(0);

  auto module = torch::nn::MultiheadAttention(options);

  module->to(c10::kQInt32);

  module->forward(
      query,
      key,
      value,
      key_padding_mask,
      false,
      attn_mask,
      false);

  return 0;
}

C10_WARP_SIZE breaks softmax/multinomial on RDNA 3.5 GPUs (gfx1151, warp_size=32)
Bug Report
Summary
On AMD RDNA 3.5 GPUs (gfx1151, e.g., Radeon 8060S / "Ryzen AI Max+" 395 integrated), torch.softmax() returns incorrect results because C10_WARP_SIZE resolves to 64 at runtime via the warpSize macro, while the hardware warp size is actually 32. This causes silent numerical corruption in any operation that relies on warp-level reductions — most critically softmax and multinomial sampling.
Reproduction
import torch
torch.cuda.init()
x = torch.randn(1, 1000, device='cuda')
s = torch.softmax(x, dim=-1).sum().item()
print(f"softmax sum: {s}")  # Expected: 1.0, Actual: ~0.5
assert s == 1.0, f"softmax sum={s}, expected 1.0 — C10_WARP_SIZE is wrong for this arch"
On an RDNA 3.5 GPU (gfx1151), this prints softmax sum: 0.5 (or similar values << 1.0) instead of the expected 1.0.
Root Cause
In c10/macros/Macros.h, the ROCm path defines:
#if defined(USE_ROCM)
#define C10_WARP_SIZE warpSize  // = 64 or 32 (Defined in hip_runtime.h)
#else
#define C10_WARP_SIZE 32
#endif
The comment says "= 64 or 32", suggesting it's runtime-adaptive. However, warpSize in HIP is a compile-time constant that resolves to 64 for all ROCm targets — even RDNA GPUs where the actual hardware warp size is 32.
This means C10_WARP_SIZE is 64 on RDNA, but warp-level primitives like WARP_SHFL_XOR(offset=WARP_SIZE/2=32) cross the real 32-lane warp boundary, corrupting parallel reductions.
Impact

Every RDNA 3.x GPU user building PyTorch from source with PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151 (or any RDNA consumer GPU)
Silent corruption: softmax returns wrong values, multinomial sampling is broken, training diverges or crashes with cryptic errors
Affects inference too — Chatterbox TTS and other models that use torch.multinomial() for sampling produce garbage output
This is the #1 blocking bug for RDNA consumer GPU users — it makes basic tensor operations subtly wrong

Environment

GPU: AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, RDNA 3.5)
ROCm: 6.4.3
PyTorch: Built from source with PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151
OS: Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0.0
HIP runtime: System libamdhip64.so.7 (via symlink from ROCm 6.4.3)

Proposed Fix
Option A (minimal, immediate): Make C10_WARP_SIZE a runtime variable for ROCm, queried from the device:
#if defined(USE_ROCM)
// warpSize is hardcoded to 64 in hip_runtime.h even on RDNA (actual warp_size=32)
// Use 32 as the safe default for consumer GPUs, or query at runtime
#define C10_WARP_SIZE 32
#else
#define C10_WARP_SIZE 32
#endif
Option B (proper, longer-term): Make C10_WARP_SIZE truly arch-aware by reading from hipDeviceAttributeWarpSize at runtime, or by using the __gfx1151__ preprocessor define to select the correct value at compile time:
#if defined(USE_ROCM)
  #if defined(__gfx1151__) || defined(__gfx1152__) || defined(__gfx1153__)
    #define C10_WARP_SIZE 32
  #else
    #define C10_WARP_SIZE 64
  #endif
#else
#define C10_WARP_SIZE 32
#endif
Note: Setting C10_WARP_SIZE=32 even on CDNA GPUs (where actual warp_size=64) should be safe — it just means warp-level primitives use the lower 32 lanes instead of all 64, which is correct for the subgroup operations PyTorch actually uses. But arch-aware selection is preferable.
Additional Context
Official ROCm PyTorch wheels also fail on RDNA 3.5 — they contain zero gfx1151 code objects, so every HIP kernel fails with hipErrorNoBinaryForGpu. Users must build from source, and building from source hits this C10_WARP_SIZE bug immediately.
Related issues:

MIOpen workspace allocation also fails on gfx1151 (every conv reports "workspace required: N, provided size: 0") — workaround is torch.backends.cudnn.enabled = False
torch.compile with reduce-overhead mode works well on RDNA once these bugs are worked around

Workaround
Patch c10/macros/Macros.h before building:
#if defined(USE_ROCM)
#define C10_WARP_SIZE 32  // RDNA 3.5 has warp_size=32
#else
#define C10_WARP_SIZE 32
#endif
Then rebuild PyTorch from source with PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151.

🐛 Describe the bug
On the torch==2.11.0+cu130 build (CUDA 13, for Blackwell / sm_120, RTX 5090), torch._inductor
registers the same Triton template and the same extern kernel twice within a single
process, hitting the hard asserts in torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py:

L1775: assert name not in self.all_templates, "duplicate template name"
L2264: assert not hasattr(extern_kernels, name), f"duplicate extern kernel: {name}"  (name=_grouped_mm)

It surfaces during vLLM 0.22.0 ModelConfig construction (pydantic) when the model architecture
is inspected — i.e. at import time, before any weights load — and crashes startup for any model:

Qwen3-VL MoE AWQ (Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration)
the tiny BAAI/bge-m3 embedding model (XLMRobertaModel)

Both fail identically, so it's not model-specific.
Versions
PyTorch version: 2.11.0+cu130
Is debug build: False
CUDA used to build PyTorch: 13.0
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64)
Python version: 3.12.4
Python platform: Linux-5.15.0-94-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
Is CUDA available: True
GPU models and configuration: GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090
Nvidia driver version: 595.58.03
cuDNN version: 9.8.0
Versions of relevant libraries:
[pip3] torch==2.11.0+cu130
[pip3] torchaudio==2.11.0+cu130
[pip3] torchvision==0.26.0+cu130
[pip3] triton==3.6.0
[pip3] (vllm==0.22.0)
Repro
vllm serve BAAI/bge-m3 --enforce-eager --trust-remote-code
→ pydantic_core.ValidationError: ... Assertion failed, duplicate template name (then, once that
template assert is bypassed, the same happens for duplicate extern kernel: _grouped_mm).
Observations / what I ruled out

Not a duplicate triton/torch install, not transformers/pydantic versions, not a stale cache/.pyc.
A clean --force-reinstall of the same torch==2.11.0+cu130 reproduces it.
Making both registrations idempotent (skip if the name is already registered, keeping the
first — they're identical on the double-import) lets vLLM load and generate correctly.
Appears specific to the +cu130 build (Blackwell); standard CUDA builds presumably don't
double-register, which is likely why it's rarely reported.

Question
Is the inductor template / extern-kernel module-level registration expected to run twice on this
build (double-import)? Should register_template / extern-kernel registration be idempotent
(skip-if-present) rather than a hard assert?

🐛 Describe the bug

### Versions

We are requesting a supported pathway or native C++ API to export models trained purely in C++ (LibTorch) directly to the AOTInductor (.pt2) format, allowing them to be loaded via torch::inductor::AOTIModelPackageLoader without requiring a Python-based graph recreation step.

Motivation
In our engineering stack, we have invested heavily in pure C++ LibTorch pipelines for both training and inference. We manage complex native memory environments, strict module inheritance architectures, and C++ specific API implementations (such as native autocast management).

Currently, AOTInductor offers incredible inference performance, and we are utilizing torch::inductor::AOTIModelPackageLoader successfully. However, the AOT compilation step (torch._export.aot_compile) is strictly bound to Python and TorchDynamo.

To bridge our pure C++ training pipeline to AOTI inference, we are forced to use a fragile workaround:

Train and save the model weights in C++ (torch::save).

Switch to Python.

Manually recreate a structurally identical torch.nn.Module.

Load the C++ weights into the Python module.

Run torch._export.aot_compile.

Switch back to C++ and load the .pt2 file via AOTIModelPackageLoader.

This cross-language weight bridging breaks the pure C++ CI/CD pipeline, introduces maintaining duplicate model definitions (one in C++, one in Python), and leaves room for human error when aligning complex layer names.

Pitch
We propose one of two potential solutions:

A Native C++ Export API: Expose a C++ function that allows a LibTorch module (which already has a defined graph) to trigger the AOT compilation backend directly, generating the .so/.pt2 package.

An Offline CLI Compiler for ScriptModules: Provide a supported Python script/CLI tool that can ingest a serialized LibTorch model (saved via C++ torch::save), trace its execution graph, and run the Triton/AOTInductor compilation pipeline without requiring the user to manually redefine the nn.Module in Python.

Alternatives
The current alternative is the manual Python "weight bridge" described above, which is difficult to scale in a strict C++ / Java-bindings engineering environment.

Additional context
We frequently benchmark local model inference on high-performance machines (e.g., M-series silicon like the M5) before deploying to production CUDA environments. Having a unified, pure C++ pipeline from training to AOT compilation to inference would significantly streamline the deployment of high-performance models in environments where embedding a Python runtime is strictly prohibited.

How to use this:
Go to the [PyTorch GitHub Issues page](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues).

Click New Issue -> Select Feature Request.

Paste the draft above.

If you have specific code snippets from your JavaCPP-PyTorch or pure C++ implementations that highlight the complexity of redefining the models, you can add them to the "Additional context" section to give the maintainers more concrete details!

Hi, nn.Linear derives from nn.Module, quite an important fact, but it is actually not mentioned at all on the doc page for nn.Linear.
There is the following issue on this page: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.11/generated/torch.nn.Linear.html

🐛 Describe the bug
AOTInductor (CUDA) miscompiles int64 aten.floor_divide when the DIVISOR is a tensor on torch.2.12:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

DEVICE = "cuda"
DIVISOR = 3

class TensorDivisorFloorDiv(nn.Module):
    """floor_divide with a 0-d int64 TENSOR divisor (the buggy case)."""

    def __init__(self, divisor: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.divisor = torch.tensor(divisor, dtype=torch.int64)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return torch.floor_divide(x, self.divisor)


class ScalarDivisorFloorDiv(nn.Module):
    """floor_divide with a python-int scalar divisor (the correct contrast)."""

    def __init__(self, divisor: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.divisor = divisor

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return torch.floor_divide(x, self.divisor)


def run_case(name: str, module: nn.Module, x: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
    module = module.to(DEVICE).eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        eager = module(x)
    ep = torch.export.export(module, (x,))
    pkg = torch._inductor.aoti_compile_and_package(ep)
    aoti = torch._inductor.aoti_load_package(pkg)(x)

    eager_l = eager.cpu().tolist()
    aoti_l = aoti.cpu().tolist()
    match = eager_l == aoti_l
    print(f"\n=== {name} ===")
    print(f"  input : {x.cpu().tolist()}")
    print(f"  eager : {eager_l}")
    print(f"  aoti  : {aoti_l}")
    print(f"  match : {match}")
    if not match:
        for xi, e, a in zip(x.cpu().tolist(), eager_l, aoti_l):
            if e != a:
                print(f"    MISMATCH: {xi} // {DIVISOR} -> eager={e}  aoti={a}")
    return match

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"torch={torch.__version__}  cuda={torch.version.cuda}  gpu={torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}")
    x = torch.tensor([-5, -1, 0, 7, 8], dtype=torch.int64, device=DEVICE)

    tensor_ok = run_case("TENSOR divisor (0-d int64)", TensorDivisorFloorDiv(DIVISOR), x)
    scalar_ok = run_case("SCALAR divisor (python int)", ScalarDivisorFloorDiv(DIVISOR), x)

    print("\n=== SUMMARY ===")
    print(f"  tensor-divisor AOTI matches eager : {tensor_ok}")
    print(f"  scalar-divisor AOTI matches eager : {scalar_ok}")
    if not tensor_ok and scalar_ok:
        print("  => REPRODUCED: AOTI miscompiles int64 floor_divide with a tensor divisor "
              "scalar divisor is correct.")
    elif tensor_ok and scalar_ok:
        print("  => NOT reproduced on this torch version (both correct).")
    else:
        print("  => Unexpected result; inspect above.")
Output:

🐛 Describe the bug
Summary
torch.matmul falls back to aten::bmm for a 3D x 2D matmul with logical shape:
lhs shape  = [384, 1, 4096]
lhs stride = (4096, 1572864, 1)
rhs shape  = [4096, 4096]

The middle dimension has size 1, so its stride should be irrelevant for memory indexing. The LHS can be flattened to [384, 4096] as a view, and explicitly doing that dispatches to aten::mm and is much faster.
This looks like a missed optimization in should_fold. The current stride check rejects this tensor because:
4096 != 1572864 * 1

But because the dimension with stride 1572864 has size 1, that stride does not affect the actual addressed elements.
Relevant source:
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/LinearAlgebra.cpp#L1988-L1998
Minimal Repro
Create repro_matmul_bs1_fold.py:
import statistics

import torch


S = 384
B = 1
H = 4096
DTYPE = torch.bfloat16
DEVICE = "cuda"


def synchronize() -> None:
    torch.cuda.synchronize()


def bench(fn, *, warmup: int = 10, reps: int = 50) -> float:
    for _ in range(warmup):
        fn()
    synchronize()

    times = []
    for _ in range(reps):
        start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        start.record()
        fn()
        end.record()
        synchronize()
        times.append(start.elapsed_time(end))
    return statistics.median(times)


def print_ops(name, fn) -> None:
    with torch.profiler.profile(
        activities=[torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CPU, torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA],
        record_shapes=True,
    ) as prof:
        fn()
        synchronize()

    interesting_ops = {
        "aten::matmul",
        "aten::mm",
        "aten::bmm",
        "aten::reshape",
        "aten::clone",
        "aten::copy_",
    }

    print(f"\n{name} ops:")
    for event in prof.key_averages(group_by_input_shape=True):
        if event.key in interesting_ops:
            print(event.key, event.input_shapes)


def main() -> None:
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise RuntimeError("CUDA is required")

    torch.manual_seed(0)

    # Logical shape [S, B, H], but with a non-contiguous size-1 batch dimension.
    # This produces shape=(384, 1, 4096), stride=(4096, 1572864, 1).
    lhs = torch.randn((B, S, H), device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE).transpose(0, 1)
    rhs = torch.randn((H, H), device=DEVICE, dtype=DTYPE)

    flattened_lhs = lhs.reshape(-1, H)

    print("device:", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))
    print("torch:", torch.__version__)
    print("cuda:", torch.version.cuda)
    print("dtype:", DTYPE)
    print("lhs shape:", tuple(lhs.shape))
    print("lhs stride:", tuple(lhs.stride()))
    print("flattened shape:", tuple(flattened_lhs.shape))
    print("flattened stride:", tuple(flattened_lhs.stride()))
    print(
        "reshape shares storage:",
        flattened_lhs.untyped_storage().data_ptr() == lhs.untyped_storage().data_ptr(),
    )

    def old_matmul() -> torch.Tensor:
        return lhs.matmul(rhs)

    def flat_matmul() -> torch.Tensor:
        return lhs.reshape(-1, H).matmul(rhs).reshape(S, B, H)

    torch.testing.assert_close(
        old_matmul().float(),
        flat_matmul().float(),
        rtol=1e-2,
        atol=1e-2,
    )

    old_ms = bench(old_matmul)
    flat_ms = bench(flat_matmul)

    print(f"\nold matmul median:  {old_ms:.3f} ms")
    print(f"flat matmul median: {flat_ms:.3f} ms")
    print(f"speedup:            {old_ms / flat_ms:.2f}x")

    print_ops("old", old_matmul)
    print_ops("flat", flat_matmul)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
Run:
python repro_matmul_bs1_fold.py
Observed Result
On an NVIDIA H100 with BF16:
device: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3
torch: 2.12.0a0+0291f960b6.nv26.04.48445190
cuda: 13.2
dtype: torch.bfloat16
lhs shape: (384, 1, 4096)
lhs stride: (4096, 1572864, 1)
flattened shape: (384, 4096)
flattened stride: (4096, 1)
reshape shares storage: True

old matmul median:  1.697 ms
flat matmul median: 0.031 ms
speedup:            54.52x

old ops:
aten::matmul [[384, 1, 4096], [4096, 4096]]
aten::reshape [[384, 1, 4096], []]
aten::reshape [[384, 4096, 4096], []]
aten::bmm [[384, 1, 4096], [384, 4096, 4096]]

flat ops:
aten::reshape [[384, 1, 4096], []]
aten::matmul [[384, 4096], [4096, 4096]]
aten::mm [[384, 4096], [4096, 4096]]
aten::reshape [[384, 4096], []]

Expected Result
For [S, 1, H] @ [H, K], torch.matmul should be able to fold the leading dimensions and dispatch to aten::mm, because the size-1 batch dimension does not affect memory indexing and flattening to [S, H] can be a view.
In this case, the fallback to batched matmul appears unnecessary and substantially slower.
Why This Matters
This pattern appears in transformer training in frozen-weight linear backward paths, where grad_output has shape [sequence, batch, hidden]. For packed or transposed layouts, the batch dimension can be size 1 but still have a non-contiguous stride. In that case, torch.matmul may dispatch to a slow batched GEMM even though an equivalent view-based flattening dispatches to a much faster mm.

🐛 Describe the bug
torch.onnx.export(..., dynamo=True) exports Tensor.masked_scatter incorrectly: the scattered source values are written in the wrong order, so the output is numerically wrong. dynamo=False (legacy exporter) is correct. It reproduces at the export shape and at other shapes, so it is not a dynamic-shape specialization issue.
import numpy as np, torch, torch.nn as nn, onnxruntime as ort

N, D = 4, 8
class M(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d):
        super().__init__()
        self.register_buffer("scale", torch.arange(d, dtype=torch.float32) + 1.0)
    def forward(self, embeds, mask, inject):     # (1,S,D), (1,S) bool, (N,D)
        return embeds.masked_scatter(mask.unsqueeze(-1), inject) * self.scale

m = M(D).eval()
embeds = torch.zeros(1, 8, D)
mask = torch.zeros(1, 8, dtype=torch.bool); mask[0, :N] = True
inject = torch.arange(N * D, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(N, D) + 1.0

for dynamo in (False, True):
    p = f"/tmp/ms_{int(dynamo)}.onnx"
    torch.onnx.export(m, (embeds, mask, inject), p,
        input_names=["embeds", "mask", "inject"], output_names=["y"],
        dynamic_axes={"embeds": {1: "S"}, "mask": {1: "S"}, "y": {1: "S"}},
        opset_version=18, dynamo=dynamo)
    o = ort.InferenceSession(p, providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"]).run(
        None, {"embeds": embeds.numpy(), "mask": mask.numpy(), "inject": inject.numpy()})[0]
    y = m(embeds, mask, inject).detach().numpy()
    print(f"{'dynamo' if dynamo else 'legacy'}: maxdiff={np.abs(o-y).max():.1f}  out[0,:6,0]={o[0,:6,0]}")
Output:
legacy: maxdiff=0.0    out[0,:6,0]=[ 1.  9. 17. 25.  0.  0.]
dynamo: maxdiff=256.0  out[0,:6,0]=[ 1.  2.  3.  4.  0.  0.]

Legacy places inject in masked_scatter order; dynamo writes the source transposed. The dynamo graph lowers masked_scatter via NonZero/ScatterND. Same result on torch 2.10.0 and 2.11.0.
Expected: dynamo=True output matches eager / dynamo=False.
Versions
PyTorch version: 2.11.0+cu128   (also reproduced on 2.10.0+cu128)
CUDA used to build PyTorch: 12.8
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64)
Python version: 3.10.20
onnxruntime 1.23.2; onnxscript installed (required by dynamo=True)
Repro is CPU-only (torch.export trace + onnxruntime CPUExecutionProvider).

Summary
On the vLLM torch-2.12 upgrade branch, the vLLM CI job "Language Models Test (Extended Pooling)" fails deterministically on test_nomic_max_model_len.py::test_use_rope_scaling_legal[model_info1] (Nomic bert_with_rope pooling model). During torch.compile warmup the AOT-compiled graph trips a stride assertion:
torch._inductor ... assert_size_stride(arg9_1, (512, 64), (64, 1))
AssertionError: expected size 8192==512, stride 64==64 at dim=0
This error most often comes from a incorrect fake (aka meta) kernel for a custom op.
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above.

The compiled graph was specialized for dim0 = 512 but is invoked with dim0 = 8192 during kernel_warmup -> flashinfer_autotune -> _dummy_run.
This passes on torch 2.11 and fails on torch 2.12 with the same vLLM commit, so torch 2.12's Inductor/AOTAutograd is the surfacing factor. Note the asserted tensor arg9_1 is a top-level graph input, not a custom-op output, so the generic "incorrect fake kernel" hint is likely misleading here.
Environment

torch 2.12.0+cu130, triton 3.7.0, torchvision 0.27.0
CUDA 13.0 (driver 580.159.03), Python 3.12.13
GPU: NVIDIA H200
vLLM branch: atalman:fix_release_212 (torch 2.12 upgrade)

Failing test
tests/models/language/pooling/test_nomic_max_model_len.py::test_use_rope_scaling_legal[model_info1]

(1 failed, 101 passed in the shard.)
Reproducibility (deterministic across fresh builds)

vLLM commit
Result

PASS

FAIL (identical)



Passes on all 5 recent main "Full CI run" builds (torch 2.11): 69423, 69310, 69146, 69110, 69077.
Bisect
The regression appeared between passing #66553 (47af9e1) and first-failing #66993 (d2792bf); the torch wheel version is identical (2.12.0+cu130) in both, so the trigger is a vLLM commit in that range:

vLLM PR #41277 "Fix error in Dynamic NTK scaling" (commit 117afeea4, 2026-05-19)

That PR changes the Dynamic-NTK RoPE cos/sin cache length in vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py:
-        max_len = self.max_position_embeddings * self.scaling_factor
-        t = torch.arange(max_len, dtype=torch.float)            # old length: 8192
+        t = torch.arange(self.max_position_embeddings, ...)     # new length: 512
The cache shrank from max_position_embeddings * scaling_factor (8192) to max_position_embeddings (512) - exactly the two sizes in expected size 8192==512. (The same PR also rewrote test_nomic_max_model_len.py and the get_rope wiring.)
Traceback (trimmed)
(EngineCore) gpu_worker.py:609 compile_or_warm_up_model -> kernel_warmup
  warmup/kernel_warmup.py:133 flashinfer_autotune -> runner._dummy_run(...)
  gpu_model_runner.py:5828 _dummy_run -> self.model(...)
  models/bert_with_rope.py:476 forward
  compilation/caching.py:217 -> compilation/piecewise_backend.py:198 compiled_graph_wrapper
  torch/_inductor/standalone_compile.py:313 __call__
  torch/_functorch/_aot_autograd/aot_autograd_result.py:723 forward
  torch/_functorch/_aot_autograd/runtime_wrappers.py:777 runtime_wrapper -> compiled_invoker.run(...)
  torch/_inductor/output_code.py:725 __call__ -> self.current_callable(inputs)
  .../inductor_cache/.../<graph>.py
    assert_size_stride(arg9_1, (512, 64), (64, 1))
AssertionError: expected size 8192==512, stride 64==64 at dim=0

Diagnosis / question
vLLM #41277 changed the RoPE cache shape (8192 -> 512), and torch 2.12's AOT/Inductor path now asserts a size mismatch that torch 2.11 tolerated on the same code. Two possibilities, and we'd appreciate maintainer input on which:

torch 2.12 Inductor/AOTAutograd regression - the compiled graph specializes dim0=512 but is invoked with 8192 (a recompile/dynamic-shape/cache-key issue), i.e. 2.12 should not be asserting here.
torch 2.12 correctly catching a latent shape inconsistency introduced by #41277 (rope cache now 512 while some buffer is still sized at the old 8192), in which case the fix is a vLLM-side correction.

What's the right interpretation of the arg9_1 (graph input) specialization at 512 vs the 8192 runtime size under torch 2.12?

🐛 Describe the bug
torch.compile with max_autotune_conv_backends = "TRITON" crashes with NoValidChoicesError for transposed convolutions (ConvTranspose2d), dilated convolutions, and any convolution configuration that the forward Triton template doesn't support.
The original issue #125728 was closed in because regular Conv2d with TRITON backend was fixed. But transposed convolutions (and dilated convolutions) hit a different code path — the forward convolution() lowering in torch/_inductor/kernel/conv.py has no ATEN fallback safety net when the Triton template guard rejects the configuration, unlike the backward path added in #178945.
Related: #151555 (feature request for full Triton conv support)
Repro
import torch
import torch._inductor.config

torch._inductor.config.max_autotune = True
torch._inductor.config.max_autotune_conv_backends = "TRITON"

class Model(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv_transpose2d = torch.nn.ConvTranspose2d(64, 128, kernel_size=(3, 5))

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.conv_transpose2d(x)

m = Model().cuda()
m_compiled = torch.compile(m)
x = torch.randn(64, 64, 128, 256, device="cuda")
out = m_compiled(x)  # NoValidChoicesError
Error
torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: LoweringException: NoValidChoicesError: No choices to select.
Provided reason: No choices exist for backend. please consider adding ATEN into
max_autotune_conv_backends config (defined in torch/_inductor/config.py) to allow at least one choice.
  target: aten.convolution.default
  args[6]: True   # transposed=True

Root Cause
The Triton template guard at conv.py:616-625 rejects transposed convolutions (and not transposed), non-unit dilation (and is_ones(dilation)), and non-zero output_padding (and is_zeros(output_padding)). When max_autotune_conv_backends = "TRITON" (no ATEN), the choices list stays empty and autotune_select_algorithm raises NoValidChoicesError.
The backward path (PR #178945) handles this correctly with a two-tier fallback. The forward path has no equivalent safety net.
Affected configurations



Configuration
Example




ConvTranspose1d
nn.ConvTranspose1d(16, 32, 3)


ConvTranspose2d
nn.ConvTranspose2d(16, 32, 3)


ConvTranspose3d
nn.ConvTranspose3d(16, 32, 3)


Conv2d dilation>1
nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, dilation=2)


ConvTranspose2d with output_padding
nn.ConvTranspose2d(16, 32, 3, stride=2, output_padding=1)



Versions
PyTorch: 2.13.0a0 (main @ ec2def0)
Triton: 3.7.0
GPU: NVIDIA H200
CUDA: 12.8

repro.py
🐛 Describe the bug
SIMDKernelFeatures.select_index_dtype() decides between tl.int32 and
tl.int64 based solely on can_use_32bit_indexing(numel, buffers),
which inspects only

the kernel's total numel, and
each buffer's storage_size.

It does not inspect the indexing expressions themselves. After
fusion, indexing expressions of the form
base + x0 + stride * x1

can carry a literal base (constant offset) whose magnitude exceeds the
int32 range [-2**31, 2**31 - 1], even when every buffer's storage_size
fits in int32. Triton then refuses to compile the generated kernel with:
ValueError: Scalar -2779057358 is out of range for type int32

A real-world trigger is slice_scatter.backward getting fused with an
mm.backward against a wide pooled embedding tensor — Inductor folds
all the slice ranges into per-load constant offsets, but the dtype
decision was already locked to int32.
Versions
Pytorch 2.12.0 + cu130 (problem exists in all versions)
PyTorch version: 2.12.0+cu130
Is debug build: False
CUDA used to build PyTorch: 13.0
ROCM used to build PyTorch: N/A
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64)
GCC version: (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0
Clang version: 14.0.0-1ubuntu1.1
CMake version: version 3.22.1
Libc version: glibc-2.35
Python version: 3.12.13 (main, Mar  4 2026, 09:23:07) [GCC 11.4.0] (64-bit runtime)
Python platform: Linux-5.15.0-117-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
Is CUDA available: True
CUDA runtime version: Could not collect
CUDA_MODULE_LOADING set to:
GPU models and configuration:
GPU 0: NVIDIA H20
GPU 1: NVIDIA H20
GPU 2: NVIDIA H20
GPU 3: NVIDIA H20
GPU 4: NVIDIA H20
GPU 5: NVIDIA H20
GPU 6: NVIDIA H20
GPU 7: NVIDIA H20
Nvidia driver version: 595.71.05
Minimal reproducer
(See attached repro.py below — pure PyTorch, no third-party deps.)
"""
Minimal reproducer: Inductor int32 address-constant overflow in fused kernels.

On unfixed builds (confirmed PyTorch 2.8.0+cu126 / Triton 3.4.0, and
current main as of 2026-05), the backward pass crashes with:

    ValueError: Scalar -2779057358 is out of range for type int32

Root cause: select_index_dtype() picks tl.int32 based solely on per-buffer
storage_size and total numel. But after fusion the address expression
becomes `base + x0 + stride*x1` where the literal `base` already exceeds
2**31. Triton refuses to compile this literal as int32.

Trigger pattern: multiple large 2-D tensors sliced at a high row offset,
concatenated on dim-1, then fed through per-column dense layers. The fused
backward kernel (slice_scatter + mm.backward) produces the oversized
constant.

Requirements:
  - CUDA GPU with ~30 GB free memory
  - PyTorch with CUDA support

Run:
    python repro.py
"""
import sys

import torch
from torch import nn


# --- Parameters chosen to trigger the three necessary conditions: ---
# (1) Each individual tensor's numel fits in int32.
# (2) The sliced working window fits in int32.
# (3) The fused address constant (SLICE_BEGIN * TOTAL_COLS) does NOT.
TOTAL_ROWS = 9_500_000
SLICE_BEGIN = 9_472_768
SLICE_END = 9_499_648
COL_WIDTHS = [32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 32, 22]  # 10 groups, sum = 310
TOTAL_COLS = sum(COL_WIDTHS)
INT32_MAX = 2**31 - 1


def check_trigger_conditions():
    """Verify the three conditions that expose the bug."""
    # (1) Largest single buffer numel fits in int32
    assert TOTAL_ROWS * max(COL_WIDTHS) < INT32_MAX, "condition 1 violated"
    # (2) Sliced window numel fits in int32
    assert (SLICE_END - SLICE_BEGIN) * TOTAL_COLS < INT32_MAX, "condition 2 violated"
    # (3) Fused address constant overflows int32
    assert SLICE_BEGIN * TOTAL_COLS > INT32_MAX, "condition 3 violated"


class SliceConcatDense(nn.Module):
    """Slice each input at a high row offset, concat, apply per-group linears."""

    def __init__(self, widths):
        super().__init__()
        self.widths = widths
        self.linears = nn.ModuleList(
            [nn.Linear(w, w, bias=False) for w in widths]
        )

    def forward(self, inputs):
        sliced = [t[SLICE_BEGIN:SLICE_END, :] for t in inputs]
        cat = torch.cat(sliced, dim=1)  # [slice_rows, TOTAL_COLS]
        out = cat.new_zeros(())
        col = 0
        for w, linear in zip(self.widths, self.linears):
            out = out + linear(cat[:, col : col + w]).sum()
            col += w
        return out


def main():
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        print("SKIP: CUDA not available", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    check_trigger_conditions()

    # Memory check: need ~2x leaf bytes (for .grad), with 1.3x safety margin
    leaf_bytes = sum(TOTAL_ROWS * w * 4 for w in COL_WIDTHS)
    need_gb = leaf_bytes * 2 / 1024**3 * 1.3
    free_gb = torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[0] / 1024**3
    if free_gb < need_gb:
        print(
            f"SKIP: need ~{need_gb:.1f} GiB free GPU memory, "
            f"have {free_gb:.1f} GiB",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2

    torch.manual_seed(0)
    inputs = [
        torch.randn(TOTAL_ROWS, w, device="cuda", requires_grad=True)
        for w in COL_WIDTHS
    ]
    model = SliceConcatDense(COL_WIDTHS).cuda()
    compiled = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False)

    try:
        loss = compiled(inputs)
        loss.backward()
    except ValueError as e:
        if "out of range for type int32" in str(e):
            print(f"BUG REPRODUCED: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        raise
    finally:
        del inputs, model, compiled
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    print("OK — no overflow (fix is effective)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())


When run on a GPU with ~30 GB free memory, the un-patched build fails in
the backward pass with the int32 ValueError above.
  File "/home/tjw378335/pytorch-main/lib/python3.12/site-packages/triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 307, in compile
    module = src.make_ir(target, options, codegen_fns, module_map, context)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/tjw378335/pytorch-main/lib/python3.12/site-packages/triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 80, in make_ir
    return ast_to_ttir(self.fn, self, context=context, options=options, codegen_fns=codegen_fns,
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: CompilationError: at 15:30:
    xindex = xoffset + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)[:]
    xmask = xindex < xnumel
    x1 = xindex // 22
    x0 = (xindex % 22)
    x2 = xindex
    tmp0 = x1
    tmp1 = tl.full([1], 9472768, tl.int64)
    tmp2 = tmp0 >= tmp1
    tmp3 = tl.full([1], 9499648, tl.int64)
    tmp4 = tmp0 < tmp3
    tmp5 = tmp2 & tmp4
    tmp6 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + ((-2936557792) + x0 + 310*x1), tmp5 & xmask, other=0.0)
                              ^
ValueError('Scalar -2936557792 is out of range for type int32')

Expected behavior
select_index_dtype() should choose tl.int64 whenever any indexing
expression's constant term is outside the int32 range, regardless of
numel / storage_size checks.
Relation to existing fixes

#157767 (drisspg, FlexAttention only) — sub-expression upcast inside
the FlexAttention kernel path. Does not affect the generic
slice_scatter / fused backward path.
#185264 (FlexAttention only) — casts pointer-arithmetic offsets to
INDEX_DTYPE inside load_checked_2d and inline pointer sites.
Both assume INDEX_DTYPE was already promoted to int64 upstream.

This issue is one layer up: the upstream dtype decision itself is
wrong, so no downstream cast can rescue it.

🐛 Describe the bug
torch.bincount with weights returns the same counts tensor in eager mode and under torch.compile(..., backend="inductor"), but calling count_nonzero() on that bincount output returns an incorrect value in the compiled path.
In the repro below, eager returns:
counts = tensor([-4.,  4.,  1., 13.,  0.,  0.])
counts.count_nonzero() = tensor(4)

Both compiled paths return the same counts tensor, but the count_nonzero result is wrong:
dynamic=False: tensor(5)
dynamic=True:  tensor(2)

This is a silent correctness issue. The intermediate tensor values match eager, but the observer count_nonzero() over that tensor returns an incorrect result in the compiled path.
Minimal reproduction
import traceback
import torch

def fn(x, weights):
    counts = x.bincount(weights=weights, minlength=6)
    nonzero_bins = counts.count_nonzero()
    return counts, nonzero_bins

x = torch.tensor([0, 2, 2, 3, 1, 0, 3, 3], dtype=torch.int64)
weights = torch.tensor([1.0, -2.0, 3.0, 0.0, 4.0, -5.0, 6.0, 7.0], dtype=torch.float32)

print("\neager")
try:
    eager = fn(x, weights)
    print("ok:", eager)
except Exception as e:
    print("error:", type(e).__name__, str(e).splitlines()[0])
    traceback.print_exc(limit=10)

for dynamic in [False, True]:
    print(f"\ncompile dynamic={dynamic}")
    try:
        torch._dynamo.reset()
        compiled = torch.compile(fn, backend="inductor", fullgraph=True, dynamic=dynamic)
        out = compiled(x, weights)
        print("ok:", out)
        if "eager" in locals():
            print("counts_equal:", torch.allclose(out[0], eager[0], atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5))
            print("nonzero_equal:", torch.equal(out[1], eager[1]))
            print("eager counts:", eager[0])
            print("compiled counts:", out[0])
            print("eager nonzero:", eager[1])
            print("compiled nonzero:", out[1])
    except Exception as e:
        print("error:", type(e).__name__, str(e).splitlines()[0])
        traceback.print_exc(limit=20)
Observed output

eager
ok: (tensor([-4.,  4.,  1., 13.,  0.,  0.]), tensor(4))

compile dynamic=False
ok: (tensor([-4.,  4.,  1., 13.,  0.,  0.]), tensor(5))
counts_equal: True
nonzero_equal: False
eager counts: tensor([-4.,  4.,  1., 13.,  0.,  0.])
compiled counts: tensor([-4.,  4.,  1., 13.,  0.,  0.])
eager nonzero: tensor(4)
compiled nonzero: tensor(5)

compile dynamic=True
ok: (tensor([-4.,  4.,  1., 13.,  0.,  0.]), tensor(2))
counts_equal: True
nonzero_equal: False
eager counts: tensor([-4.,  4.,  1., 13.,  0.,  0.])
compiled counts: tensor([-4.,  4.,  1., 13.,  0.,  0.])
eager nonzero: tensor(4)
compiled nonzero: tensor(2)

Expected behavior
counts.count_nonzero() should return the same value as eager mode.
Expected:
tensor(4)

for both dynamic=False and dynamic=True.
Actual behavior
The compiled path returns incorrect count_nonzero values even though the counts tensor itself matches eager:
dynamic=False: tensor(5)
dynamic=True:  tensor(2)

Versions
PyTorch version: 2.10.0+cpu

🐛 Describe the bug
torch.linalg.cond(x, p="fro") works in eager mode and also works with torch.compile(..., backend="inductor", dynamic=False, fullgraph=True).
However, the same function fails when compiled with dynamic=True. The failure happens during Dynamo fake tensor execution with symbolic sizes:
RuntimeError: Cannot call numel() on tensor with symbolic sizes/strides

The failing fake tensor call is:
torch.linalg.cond(FakeTensor(..., size=(s77, s77)), p="fro")

This looks like a dynamic-shape / fake-tensor issue in the torch.linalg.cond(p="fro") path. Static-shape compilation succeeds, but dynamic-shape compilation fails before Inductor lowering.
Expected behavior: dynamic=True compilation should either compile and return the same result as eager/static-shape compile, or graph-break/fallback cleanly. It should not fail during fake tensor execution because linalg.cond calls numel() on a symbolic-size tensor.
Actual behavior: dynamic=True compilation fails with TorchRuntimeError: RuntimeError when making fake tensor call.
import traceback
import torch

def fn(x):
    condition_number = torch.linalg.cond(x, p="fro")
    observer = (
        condition_number > torch.tensor(0.0, dtype=condition_number.dtype)
    ).count_nonzero()
    return condition_number, observer

x = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]], dtype=torch.float32)

print("\neager")
try:
    out = fn(x)
    print("ok:", out)
except Exception as e:
    print("error:", type(e).__name__, str(e).splitlines()[0])
    traceback.print_exc(limit=10)

print("\ncompile dynamic=False")
try:
    torch._dynamo.reset()
    compiled = torch.compile(fn, backend="inductor", dynamic=False, fullgraph=True)
    out = compiled(x)
    print("ok:", out)
except Exception as e:
    print("error:", type(e).__name__, str(e).splitlines()[0])
    traceback.print_exc(limit=20)

print("\ncompile dynamic=True")
try:
    torch._dynamo.reset()
    compiled = torch.compile(fn, backend="inductor", dynamic=True, fullgraph=True)
    out = compiled(x)
    print("ok:", out)
except Exception as e:
    print("error:", type(e).__name__, str(e).splitlines()[0])
    traceback.print_exc(limit=20)
Observed output:
eager
ok: (tensor(15.0000), tensor(1))

compile dynamic=False
ok: (tensor(15.0000), tensor(1))

compile dynamic=True
error: TorchRuntimeError RuntimeError when making fake tensor call

Relevant error excerpt:
Dynamo failed to run FX node with fake tensors:
call_function <built-in function linalg_cond>(
    *(FakeTensor(..., size=(s77, s77)),),
    **{'p': 'fro'}
)

RuntimeError: Cannot call numel() on tensor with symbolic sizes/strides

Versions
PyTorch version: 2.10.0+cpu

🐛 Describe the bug
Summary
Exporting the joint of a model that calls local_map (with
local_map.defer_inlining() so the HOP is captured) works fine when the
local_map call is at the top level, but fails when the call is wrapped in a
nested_compile_region (i.e. captured as an invoke_subgraph HOP).
Two distinct errors occur:

KeyError: 'is_backward'
After working around (1): AttributeError: module 'torch._higher_order_ops.local_map' has no attribute 'call_local_map'

Repro
import contextlib
from contextlib import ExitStack

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.distributed.device_mesh import init_device_mesh
from torch.distributed.tensor.experimental import local_map
from torch.distributed.tensor.placement_types import Shard

WORLD, MESH_SHAPE, MESH_DIMS = 4, (2, 2), ("dp", "sp")
PLACEMENT = (Shard(0), Shard(1))


def setup_mesh():
    from torch.testing._internal.distributed.fake_pg import FakeStore
    torch.distributed.init_process_group("fake", store=FakeStore(), rank=0, world_size=WORLD)
    return init_device_mesh("cpu", MESH_SHAPE, mesh_dim_names=MESH_DIMS)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def deferred_local_map_capture():
    from torch._dynamo.variables.higher_order_ops import (
        LocalMapWrappedHigherOrderVariable as vt_cls,
    )
    from torch._higher_order_ops import local_map as local_map_module
    with vt_cls.enable(), local_map_module.defer_inlining():
        yield


class Inner(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim, mesh):
        super().__init__()
        self.lin = nn.Linear(dim, dim, bias=False)
        self.mesh = mesh

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.lin(x)

        def ident(t):
            return t.clone()  # HOP disallows input->output aliasing

        return local_map(
            ident,
            out_placements=(PLACEMENT,),
            in_placements=(PLACEMENT,),
            device_mesh=self.mesh,
            redistribute_inputs=True,
        )(x)


class NestedRegion(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, layer):
        super().__init__()
        self.layer = layer

    @torch.compiler.nested_compile_region
    def forward(self, *a, **k):
        return self.layer(*a, **k)


def run_export(model, x):
    from torch._dynamo.functional_export import dynamo_graph_capture_for_export
    from torch._functorch.aot_autograd import aot_export_joint_with_descriptors
    with deferred_local_map_capture():
        gm = dynamo_graph_capture_for_export(model)(x)
        with ExitStack() as stack:
            aot_export_joint_with_descriptors(stack, gm, (x,))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mesh = setup_mesh()
    x = torch.randn(8, 32, 16, requires_grad=True)

    inner = Inner(16, mesh)
    run_export(inner, x)            # top-level local_map: OK
    print("top-level: OK")

    torch._dynamo.reset()
    run_export(NestedRegion(inner), x)   # nested_compile_region: KeyError: 'is_backward'
Root cause
The deferred-inlining path in torch/_higher_order_ops/local_map.py assumes the
local_map_hop sits at the top level of the captured graph. nested_compile_region
wraps it in invoke_subgraph, which (a) runs its subgraph body below autograd and
(b) re-emits the subgraph as Python source. Neither is handled.
Error 1 — KeyError: 'is_backward' (fake_mode_key, ~line 565):
is_backward = gm.meta["is_backward"]
is_backward / num_activations are only populated by create_hop_fw_bw, which
only runs from the Autograd dispatch key. When the HOP is nested inside
invoke_subgraph, the subgraph runs below autograd, so that key never fires and
the meta is never set.
Error 2 — AttributeError: ... 'call_local_map' (proxy_mode_key, ~line 628):
def call_local_map(*_args, **_kwargs):                 # nested closure
    return functools.partial(local_map_hop, gm)(*_args, **_kwargs)
This closure is used as the FX call_function target. When invoke_subgraph
re-emits its subgraph as source, FX serializes the target via func.__name__
(dropping the <locals> qualname), producing
torch._higher_order_ops.local_map.call_local_map — which is not a real module
attribute. (At top level the graph isn't re-serialized to source, so this never
bites.)
Suggested fix

Error 1: in fake_mode_key, default the meta for an un-partitioned (pure
forward) graph, e.g. gm.meta.get("is_backward", False) and
gm.meta.get("num_activations", 0).
Error 2: make the proxied target a real, importable module-level callable
(e.g. thread gm through as a get_attr arg with local_map_hop as the
target), instead of a <locals> closure. The existing
# TODO: get rid of this when we can install as a subgraph comment points at
this spot.

With both applied, the nested export succeeds and produces a well-formed joint
(forward + backward).
Versions
PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu128
cc @chauhang @penguinwu @wanchaol @tianyu-l @wz337 @XilunWu @d4l3k @pragupta @SherlockNoMad @ppwwyyxx @weifengpy @ydwu4 @bdhirsh @bobrenjc93 @aorenste

Minimal repro:

import logging
import time
import torch
import torch._inductor.exc as exc

logging.getLogger("torch._inductor.graph").setLevel(logging.WARNING)

orig = exc.MissingOperatorWithoutDecomp.operator_str
calls = 0
format_time = 0.0
lengths = []

def timed_operator_str(target, args, kwargs):
    global calls, format_time
    calls += 1
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        s = orig(target, args, kwargs)
        lengths.append(len(s))
        return s
    finally:
        format_time += time.perf_counter() - t0

exc.MissingOperatorWithoutDecomp.operator_str = staticmethod(timed_operator_str)

N = 80
ops = []
for i in range(N):
    @torch.library.custom_op(f"reprochain::clone_{i}", mutates_args=())
    def op(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return x.clone()

    @op.register_fake
    def _(x):
        return torch.empty_like(x)

    ops.append(getattr(torch.ops.reprochain, f"clone_{i}"))

def f(x):
    for op in ops:
        x = op(x)
    return x

t0 = time.perf_counter()
torch.compile(f, backend="inductor", fullgraph=True)(torch.randn(4))
print({
    "total_s": time.perf_counter() - t0,
    "operator_str_calls": calls,
    "operator_str_s": format_time,
    "last_string_len": lengths[-1],
})

On my local torch 2.11.0+cu130, this printed about 2.6s spent only in operator_str, with the final diagnostic string
around 683k chars, despite the logger being at WARNING.
Suggested upstream fix: guard the diagnostic formatting in torch/_inductor/graph.py with
log.isEnabledFor(logging.INFO) or otherwise avoid calling error.operator_str(...) unless the message will actually be
emitted.
To be clear, this issue is codex-generated.

🐛 Describe the bug
Description
When using mixed precision training (mixed_fp16) with DDP distributed strategy and SGD optimizer, training fails with RuntimeError: Non-finite gradient detected even though gradient clipping is properly configured (clip_grad_norm=1.0).
According to PyTorch documentation, GradScaler should automatically skip updates and adjust the scale when non-finite gradients are detected, allowing training to continue. However, in this configuration, training terminates with an error instead of recovering.
To Reproduce
Minimal reproduction configuration:
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from torch.nn.parallel import DistributedDataParallel as DDP
from torch.cuda.amp import GradScaler, autocast
import torchvision.models as models

# Training configuration
config = {
    "model": "resnet18",
    "optimizer": "sgd",
    "learning_rate": 0.1,
    "precision": "mixed_fp16",
    "amp_enabled": True,
    "amp_dtype": torch.float16,
    "grad_scaler_enabled": True,
    "clip_grad_norm": 1.0,
    "distributed_strategy": "ddp",
    "backend": "nccl",
    "gradient_accumulation_steps": 2,
    "global_batch_size": 4,
    "per_device_batch_size": 1,
    "weight_decay": 0.0001,
    "seed": 0,
    "deterministic": True
}

# Initialize distributed training
dist.init_process_group(backend="nccl")
torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)

# Model setup
model = models.resnet18(num_classes=10).cuda()
model = DDP(model)

# Optimizer
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(
    model.parameters(),
    lr=config["learning_rate"],
    weight_decay=config["weight_decay"]
)

# GradScaler for mixed precision
scaler = GradScaler()

# Training loop
for batch in dataloader:
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    
    with autocast(dtype=torch.float16):
        outputs = model(batch["input"])
        loss = criterion(outputs, batch["target"])
    
    scaler.scale(loss).backward()
    scaler.unscale_(optimizer)
    torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), config["clip_grad_norm"])
    scaler.step(optimizer)
    scaler.update()
Expected behavior
According to the PyTorch AMP documentation, GradScaler should:

Detect non-finite gradients during unscale_
Skip the optimizer step
Reduce the loss scale
Continue training

The training should not terminate with an error but should handle the overflow gracefully.
Actual behavior
Training fails after 52 steps with:
RuntimeError: Non-finite gradient detected

Full error traceback:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/root/pyprojects/confFuzzDL/L2_ST/pt_l2_runner.py", line 684, in run_one

  File "/root/pyprojects/confFuzzDL/L2_ST/pt_l2_runner.py", line 596, in l2_worker
    grad_norm = finite_grad_norm(model)
                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/root/pyprojects/confFuzzDL/L2_ST/pt_l2_runner.py", line 364, in finite_grad_norm
    raise RuntimeError("Non-finite gradient detected")
RuntimeError: Non-finite gradient detected

Training progress before failure:
Step 48: loss=1.814453, grad_norm=25.662022
Step 49: loss=1.027344, grad_norm=8.908818
Step 50: loss=0.989746, grad_norm=13.826459
Step 51: loss=0.228394, grad_norm=6.302933
Step 52: loss=0.029541, grad_norm=16.247002
Step 53: Non-finite gradient detected (FAILED)

The training terminates instead of recovering from the overflow. Note that gradient norms were finite and reasonable (6-26 range) right before the failure.

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
torch._inductor.fx_passes.node_runtime_estimation._log_compute_estimations builds each per-compute-node CSV row with four .4f format specs:
torch/_inductor/fx_passes/node_runtime_estimation.py (main @ today)
312:    rows = [
313:        f"{est_b * 1e3:.4f}",
314:        f"{est_a * 1e3:.4f}",
315:        f"{(est_a / est_b) if est_b > 0 else 0:.4f}",
316:        f"{(est_a - est_b) * 1e3:.4f}",
317:        ...

SymFloat.__format__ only accepts the empty format spec, so the moment any est_a or est_b is a torch.SymFloat, one of those four cells raises:
TypeError: unsupported format string passed to SymFloat.__format__

surfaced as torch._inductor.exc.InductorError from compile_fx_inner. The rows list is built eagerly (trace_structured's payload_fn=lambda: log_str only defers the artifact emission, not the construction of log_str), so the crash fires every time _log_compute_estimations is reached with a symbolic estimate, regardless of TORCH_LOGS.
When this triggers in production
_log_compute_estimations is called from OverlapScheduler._align_compute_nodes_runtime_estimations_across_all_distributed_ranks (in torch/_inductor/fx_passes/overlap_scheduling.py). All of the following have to be true for it to crash:

Inductor backend, overlap scheduling on. torch._inductor.config.aten_distributed_optimizations.enable_overlap_scheduling = True — this is what makes the post_grad overlap_scheduling pass run and call _log_compute_estimations at all.
At least one collective in the compiled graph. The pass short-circuits via if not any(is_wait_tensor(n) for n in gm.graph.nodes): return gm; without a collective _log_compute_estimations is never reached. In practice this just means a real distributed training step (any all_gather / reduce_scatter / all_to_all_single etc. baked into the compiled region).
Dynamic shapes, or any other source of symbolic compute-node inputs — so the runtime estimate of at least one compute node can be symbolic. torch.compile(..., dynamic=True), automatic dynamic on the second recompile, or unbacked symbols from data-dependent ops all qualify.
The estimator hands _log_compute_estimations a SymFloat. The two natural paths that do this are:

The analytical roofline path: get_compute_time returns flop_count / peak_empirical_flops, where flop_count from flop_registry[aten.mm] is a SymInt under dynamic shapes — so compute_time is a SymFloat. On compute-bound ops max(transfer_time, compute_time) keeps the SymFloat, and it flows straight into the analytical column. This is the original LTX-2.3 crash on PT 2.11; production hits it whenever a matmul with a symbolic dim is arithmetic-intensity-heavy enough to be compute-bound on the target accelerator (e.g. (s, 4096) @ (4096, 4096)).
A custom_runtime_estimation callback that returns a SymFloat (e.g. one derived from node.meta["val"].shape[0] for size-dependent timing models).



The original landing was xDiT / LTX-2.3 with ulysses_degree=8: dynamic shapes + Inductor overlap scheduling + a joint video+audio transformer block whose compute-bound aten.mm.default nodes had a symbolic sequence dim. The minimal reproducer below exhibits the same crash without needing any of that infrastructure.
Reproducer
import torch
import torch.fx as fx
from torch.fx.experimental.symbolic_shapes import ShapeEnv
from torch._inductor.fx_passes.node_runtime_estimation import _log_compute_estimations

shape_env = ShapeEnv()
sf = shape_env.create_unbacked_symint() / 2.0   # torch.SymFloat

g = fx.Graph()
n = g.placeholder("x")
n.meta["val"] = torch.empty(0)

_log_compute_estimations(
    compute_nodes=[n],
    benchmarked_estimations=[0.1],
    analytical_estimations=[sf],
)
# -> TypeError: unsupported format string passed to SymFloat.__format__
Full self-contained script: repro_minimal.py runs with plain python repro_minimal.py and demonstrates both the primitive (f"{sf:.4f}") and the exact _log_compute_estimations call-site failure
Suggested fix
_log_compute_estimations is purely a logging helper — the values being formatted never feed back into scheduling decisions. Coerce each value to float before formatting, with a str() fallback for symbolic values that can't be hinted:
def _fmt(v) -> str:
    try:
        return f"{float(v):.4f}"
    except (TypeError, RuntimeError):
        return str(v)

rows = [
    [
        _node_summary(node),
        _fmt(est_b * 1e3),
        _fmt(est_a * 1e3),
        _fmt((est_a / est_b) if est_b > 0 else 0),
        _fmt((est_a - est_b) * 1e3),
        str(count_flops_fx(node)),
    ]
    for node, est_b, est_a in zip(
        compute_nodes, benchmarked_estimations, analytical_estimations
    )
]
This is defensive against every present and future caller and doesn't depend on each upstream estimator remembering to hint.

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
When a local_map region is nested inside a torch.compiler.nested_compile_region
(i.e. a local_map_hop ends up inside an invoke_subgraph body) and the graph is
exported for autograd via aot_export_joint_with_descriptors with
local_map's deferred inlining enabled, export fails during forward
metadata collection.
There are two independent failures:

KeyError: 'is_backward' — the nested local_map_hop reaches fake_mode_key
without having gone through its autograd key, so the fw/bw-split metadata it
expects was never stamped.
After working around (1): AttributeError: module 'torch._higher_order_ops.local_map' has no attribute 'call_local_map'
— proxy_mode_key records the node target as a local closure, which
invoke_subgraph cannot resolve when it replays/re-traces the captured body.

A top-level local_map (no nested_compile_region) works fine; only the nested
combination breaks.
Minimal reproduction
Self-contained (torch-only, FakeStore, CPU). Demonstrates all three cases:
top-level OK, nested -> Layer 1, nested + Layer-1-workaround -> Layer 2.
import contextlib
from contextlib import ExitStack

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.distributed.device_mesh import init_device_mesh
from torch.distributed.tensor.experimental import local_map
from torch.distributed.tensor.placement_types import Shard

WORLD, MESH_SHAPE, MESH_DIMS = 4, (2, 2), ("dp", "sp")
PLACEMENT = (Shard(0), Shard(1))  # dp: batch-shard, sp: seq-shard


def setup_mesh():
    from torch.testing._internal.distributed.fake_pg import FakeStore
    torch.distributed.init_process_group(
        "fake", store=FakeStore(), rank=0, world_size=WORLD
    )
    return init_device_mesh("cpu", MESH_SHAPE, mesh_dim_names=MESH_DIMS)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def deferred_local_map_capture():
    # How we drives local_map: defer inlining (-> trace with local
    # shapes) and let Dynamo capture local_map as the local_map_hop.
    from torch._dynamo.variables.higher_order_ops import (
        LocalMapWrappedHigherOrderVariable as vt_cls,
    )
    from torch._higher_order_ops import local_map as local_map_module
    with vt_cls.enable(), local_map_module.defer_inlining():
        yield


class Inner(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim, mesh):
        super().__init__()
        self.lin = nn.Linear(dim, dim, bias=False)
        self.mesh = mesh

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.lin(x)

        def ident(t):
            return t.clone()  # local_map HOP disallows input->output aliasing

        return local_map(
            ident,
            out_placements=(PLACEMENT,),
            in_placements=(PLACEMENT,),
            device_mesh=self.mesh,
            redistribute_inputs=True,
        )(x)


class NestedRegion(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, layer):
        super().__init__()
        self.layer = layer

    @torch.compiler.nested_compile_region
    def forward(self, *a, **k):
        return self.layer(*a, **k)


class Model(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim, mesh, nested):
        super().__init__()
        inner = Inner(dim, mesh)
        self.block = NestedRegion(inner) if nested else inner

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.block(x)


def run_export(model, x):
    from torch._dynamo.functional_export import dynamo_graph_capture_for_export
    from torch._functorch.aot_autograd import aot_export_joint_with_descriptors
    with deferred_local_map_capture():
        gm = dynamo_graph_capture_for_export(model)(x)
        with ExitStack() as stack:
            aot_export_joint_with_descriptors(stack, gm, (x,))


def layer1_workaround():
    # Probe only: default the missing fw/bw-split meta so the *next* (Layer 2)
    # failure surfaces. NOT a correct fix.
    import torch._higher_order_ops.local_map as lm
    from torch._subclasses.fake_tensor import FakeTensorMode
    tbl = lm.local_map_hop.python_key_table
    orig = tbl[FakeTensorMode]

    def patched(mode, gm, *args, **kwargs):
        if lm._DEFER_INLINING and "is_backward" not in getattr(gm, "meta", {}):
            gm.meta.setdefault("is_backward", False)
            gm.meta.setdefault("num_activations", 0)
        return orig(mode, gm, *args, **kwargs)

    tbl[FakeTensorMode] = patched


def root(e):
    cur, d = e, 0
    while cur.__cause__ is not None and d < 16:
        cur, d = cur.__cause__, d + 1
    return cur


def first_line(r):
    # KeyError stringifies via repr(), embedding fx context as escaped "\n".
    return f"{type(r).__name__}: {str(r).split(chr(92) + 'n')[0].splitlines()[0][:80]}"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mesh = setup_mesh()
    x = torch.randn(8, 32, 16, requires_grad=True)
    for nested in (False, True):
        torch._dynamo.reset()
        try:
            run_export(Model(16, mesh, nested), x)
            print(f"nested={nested}: OK")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"nested={nested}: {first_line(root(e))}")

    layer1_workaround()
    torch._dynamo.reset()
    try:
        run_export(Model(16, mesh, True), x)
        print("nested=True + layer1 workaround: OK")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"nested=True + layer1 workaround: {first_line(root(e))}")
Output
nested=False: OK
nested=True: KeyError: 'is_backward
nested=True + layer1 workaround: AttributeError: module 'torch._higher_order_ops.local_map' has no attribute 'call_local_map'

Expected behavior
Exporting the joint for a local_map region nested inside a
nested_compile_region should succeed (or raise a clear, intentional
"unsupported" error), just like a top-level local_map does.
Actual behavior and root cause
Layer 1 — KeyError: 'is_backward'
Stack (abridged):
aot_export_joint_with_descriptors
  -> run_functionalized_fw_and_collect_metadata     # forward metadata pass
  -> Interpreter.run() executes the invoke_subgraph node
  -> body's local_map_hop -> fake_mode_key
  -> is_backward = gm.meta["is_backward"]            # KeyError
     torch/_higher_order_ops/local_map.py  (fake_mode_key)

fake_mode_key (under _DEFER_INLINING=True) reads gm.meta["is_backward"]
and gm.meta["num_activations"]. Those keys are only stamped by
autograd_key -> create_hop_fw_bw (which partitions the region into fw/bw
GraphModules and sets the meta).
But InvokeSubgraphAutogradOp.forward runs the body under
torch._C._AutoDispatchBelowAutograd()
(torch/_higher_order_ops/invoke_subgraph.py), so the nested local_map_hop
never dispatches through its autograd key. create_hop_fw_bw never runs and
the meta is missing. Confirmed by printing the nested subgraph meta:
gm.meta keys = ['local_map_kwargs']     # is_backward / num_activations are absent

(local_map_kwargs survives because Dynamo's LocalMapWrappedHigherOrderVariable
sets it at capture time.)
Layer 2 — AttributeError: ... 'call_local_map'
After defaulting the Layer-1 meta, export proceeds and then fails when
invoke_subgraph replays / re-traces its captured body:
register_fake(invoke_subgraph) -> subgraph(*operands)     # invoke_subgraph.py
  -> generated code: torch._higher_order_ops.local_map.call_local_map(...)
  -> AttributeError: module has no attribute 'call_local_map'

proxy_mode_key records the node target as a closure defined inside the
function:
# torch/_higher_order_ops/local_map.py, proxy_mode_key
def call_local_map(*_args, **_kwargs):
    return functools.partial(local_map_hop, gm)(*_args, **_kwargs)
# (there is already a "TODO: get rid of this when we can install as a subgraph")
At top level this works because the FX graph keeps the actual callable and is
never re-resolved by name. But invoke_subgraph captures the body as a reusable
subgraph and replays/re-traces it (register_fake -> subgraph(*operands),
and reenter_make_fx(subgraph)(*operands) in the proxy impl); the generated code
references the target by qualified name torch._higher_order_ops.local_map.call_local_map,
which does not exist (the closure also bound gm, so a module-level function
could not recover it from the call args anyway).
What works as a probe (not a fix)
Both failures can be worked around locally:

Layer 1: in fake_mode_key, when is_backward is absent treat the gm as a
forward body (is_backward=False, num_activations=0). The real fw/bw split
still happens inside invoke_subgraph's own joint, so backward stays correct.
Layer 2: stash the call_local_map closure under a unique module-level name so
FX codegen emits a resolvable reference.

With both probes, an end-to-end FSDP+Ulysses-SP model (nested_compile_region
per transformer layer, local_map for the seq<->head all-to-all inside
attention) compiles and produces a correct graph: forward seq->head
all-to-all + backward head->seq all-to-all (exact inverse), all communication
localized inside the regions. So the two HOPs can compose; the blockers are the
two assumptions above.
Versions
PyTorch version: 2.11.0+cu128            # git 70d99e998b4955e0049d13a98d77ae1b14db1f45
Is debug build: False
CUDA used to build PyTorch: 12.8
OS: Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) (x86_64)
Python version: 3.11.2
Is CUDA available: False                 # repro runs on CPU via the fake process group
[pip3] numpy==2.4.4
[pip3] torch==2.11.0+cu128

cc @chauhang @penguinwu @ydwu4 @bdhirsh @bobrenjc93 @aorenste @xmfan @yanboliang

🐛 Describe the bug
possible bug / numerical inconsistency under torch.compile. I am not sure if it is a bug. Can you help check? Here is an example
import torch
import torchvision.transforms.v2.functional as F
from torchvision.transforms import InterpolationMode

device = "cuda"
new_size = (48, 48)
interpolation = InterpolationMode.BILINEAR

def resize_uint8(x):
    return F.resize(x, new_size, interpolation=interpolation, antialias=False)

compiled_resize_uint8 = torch.compile(resize_uint8, mode="reduce-overhead")

for seed in range(10):
    torch.compiler.reset()
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    image = torch.randint(0, 255, (1, 3, 224, 224), dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
    eager = resize_uint8(image)
    compiled = compiled_resize_uint8(image)

    diff = eager.to(torch.int16) - compiled.to(torch.int16)
    print(
        seed,
        "mismatch:",
        (diff != 0).sum().item(),
        "max_abs:",
        diff.abs().max().item(),
    )

    if (diff != 0).any():
        idx = (diff != 0).nonzero()[0].tolist()
        print("first mismatch:", idx, eager[tuple(idx)].item(), compiled[tuple(idx)].item())

Our expectation: torch.compile should not change the eager output of torchvision.transforms.v2.functional.resize for the same uint8 input, especially when the output is still uint8, even if the difference is only a few pixels by 1 stop, it will cause the strict equivalence test to fail.

🐛 Describe the bug
Issue
There's an issue with SequentialLR(..., milestones=[0, ...]). 
We use this sometimes to test with no warmup.

In init

It initializes the learning rate with the FIRST scheduler, regardless of what the milestones specify.


Then in the step function:

last_epoch is immediately incremented to 1
It then fetches the CORRECT scheduler by running a bisect_right to get the correct idx. In this case, idx is 1, so it gets the second scheduler.
It should ideally update the learning rate immediately by entering if idx > 0 and self._milestones[idx - 1] == self.last_epoch:
[BUG HERE] But in this case, right after init, self._milestones[idx - 1] is 0 and self.last_epoch is 1, so the equality fails, and it goes straight to the else block, and runs scheduler.step.
This runs the correct scheduler, but with the initial learning rate set by the first scheduler.



Reproducing
Script
import torch
import torch.optim as optim
from torch import nn
from torch.optim.lr_scheduler import LinearLR, SequentialLR

model = nn.Linear(10, 10)
optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1.0)

warmup = LinearLR(optimizer, start_factor=0.1, end_factor=0.5, total_iters=10)
decay = LinearLR(optimizer, start_factor=0.5, end_factor=0.1, total_iters=10)
scheduler = SequentialLR(optimizer, schedulers=[warmup, decay], milestones=[0])

print("Initial LR:", scheduler.get_last_lr()[0])
for _ in range(10):
    scheduler.step()
    print("Step LR:", scheduler.get_last_lr()[0])

nodes.bodyText:
Question: should torch.compile materialize slice.contiguous() when contiguity depends on a symbolic size?
Summary
I am seeing a larger compiled CUDA graph return a logical slice with the original padded physical row stride even though the source graph contains an explicit .contiguous() on that slice. I would like to confirm the intended PyTorch semantics for this case, because the answer determines whether this should be handled in Inductor or whether the affected downstream callee/operator must explicitly request or materialize compact layout.
The standalone slice-only probe below does not reproduce the issue in a local Docker source-validation environment. That environment reports PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, and Triton 3.6.0.
The simple probe preserves compact strides across the standard torch.compile backend ablations in that environment. That suggests the real trigger requires more of the larger graph context, such as a custom op result, a piecewise compiled subgraph return, a downstream callee/operator layout requirement, or the way symbolic layout information is propagated across that boundary.
Why The Size-1 Case Matters
The nuance is that PyTorch ignores size-1 dimensions when checking contiguity. That means a tensor with shape (1, 4640) and stride (4672, 1) can be contiguous: there is only one row, so the row stride is never used to step from one logical row to the next.
For shape (72, 4640), the same stride is not contiguous: each logical row has 4640 elements, but the next row starts 4672 elements later, leaving a physical gap after every row.
Observed eager behavior in the PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 Docker environment:
shape (1, 4640),  stride (4672, 1): is_contiguous=True,
  contiguous() returns the same storage
shape (2, 4640),  stride (4672, 1): is_contiguous=False,
  contiguous() returns stride (4640, 1)
shape (72, 4640), stride (4672, 1): is_contiguous=False,
  contiguous() returns stride (4640, 1)

This matches the implementation in torch/_prims_common/__init__.py:
# This function is equivalent to compute_contiguous() from TensorImpl.cpp
def is_contiguous(a):
    ...
    for x, y in reversed(tuple(zip(a.shape, a.stride()))):
        # Skips checking strides when a dimension has length 1
        if guard_size_oblivious(x == 1):
            continue
        if guard_size_oblivious(y != expected_stride):
            return False
        expected_stride = expected_stride * x
    return True
The reference implementation of contiguous() in torch/_refs/__init__.py uses that contiguity predicate and otherwise clones:
def contiguous(a, *, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format):
    if utils.is_contiguous_for_memory_format(a, memory_format=memory_format):
        return a
    return torch.clone(a, memory_format=memory_format)
So my current interpretation is:

If Inductor can prove or guard that the leading dimension is 1, preserving the padded row stride is acceptable.
If the leading dimension is symbolic and can be greater than 1, preserving (4672, 1) after .contiguous() is not generally equivalent to eager PyTorch semantics.

Please confirm whether that interpretation matches the intended compiler contract.
Standalone Semantic Probe
This probe checks the simple slice.contiguous() behavior without the larger custom-op graph context:
import torch


def f(x):
    y = x[:, :4640].contiguous()
    return y


for backend in [
    "eager",
    "aot_eager",
    "aot_eager_decomp_partition",
    "inductor",
]:
    for dynamic in [None, False, True]:
        compiled = torch.compile(f, backend=backend, dynamic=dynamic)
        x = torch.empty_strided(
            (72, 4672),
            (4672, 1),
            device="cuda",
            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        )
        y = compiled(x)
        print(backend, dynamic, tuple(y.shape), y.stride(), y.is_contiguous())
        assert tuple(y.shape) == (72, 4640)
        assert y.stride() == (4640, 1)
        assert y.is_contiguous()
Docker result with PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130: all backend/dynamic combinations on CPU and CUDA returned compact stride (4640, 1) and is_contiguous=True.
That means this small probe confirms the expected semantics in the same PyTorch line as the source-validation image, but it does not reproduce the larger compiled-graph failure by itself.
Observed In A Larger Compiled Graph
The larger graph where this was observed has a custom CUDA op that returns a physically padded matrix with shape (s72, 4672). The model code slices it to logical width 4640 and calls .contiguous() before returning from a compiled subgraph.
The source FX graph contains:
marlin_gemm: bf16[s72, 4672] = torch.ops._C.marlin_gemm(..., None, ...)
getitem: bf16[s72, 4640] = marlin_gemm[..., :4640]
contiguous: bf16[s72, 4640] = getitem.contiguous()

The passing compiled artifact contains an explicit clone/copy-slice materialization:
buf8 = empty_strided_cuda((s72, 4640), (4640, 1), torch.bfloat16)
triton_poi_fused_clone_slice_2.run(buf7, buf8, 4640*s72, stream=stream0)
return (buf8, ...)

The failing compiled artifact omits that materialization and returns a padded-stride reinterpretation:
return (reinterpret_tensor(buf7, (s72, 4640), (4672, 1), 0), ...)

In the failing vLLM path, the relevant code is in:
vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py

The FP8 Marlin W8A16 projection output is split, sliced, and fed through Mamba mixer, normalization, and SSD logic under torch.compile. A raw-slice diagnostic, described below, passes through this same path. That means I do not currently have evidence that a specific Mamba callee/operator is unable to consume the padded-stride structure; the failure is tied to the .contiguous() path itself.
The generated artifact difference remains the key point. The FX graph contains the explicit compaction request:
marlin_gemm: bf16[s72, 4672] = torch.ops._C.marlin_gemm(..., None, ...)
getitem: bf16[s72, 4640] = marlin_gemm[..., :4640]
contiguous: bf16[s72, 4640] = getitem.contiguous()

But the failing emitted callable still returns padded-stride views:
return (reinterpret_tensor(buf7, (s72, 4640), (4672, 1), 0),
        buf0,
        reinterpret_tensor(buf7, (s72, 2048), (4672, 1), 0),
        buf3)

Raw-Slice Diagnostic Result
I also ran a local discriminator in the full A100/SM80 serving graph. It replaced the producer-side expression:
output = output[..., :size_n].contiguous()
with:
output = output[..., :size_n]
This leaves the downstream path consuming the raw logical slice rather than an attempted .contiguous() result. Under the same serving configuration, this run passed the deterministic sanity requests:
RESPONSE capital_japan: content='Tokyo'
RESPONSE math: content='42'
PASS vllm_serve_sanity

That result is why I am not claiming that a specific Mamba callee/operator is currently proven to require compact layout. The downstream path can consume the raw padded-stride logical slice in this graph. The failing condition is tied to the presence/lowering/effect of .contiguous() on the sliced padded-stride tensor.
Public vLLM Reproducer
I created public vLLM fork branches that assemble the vLLM-side prerequisites needed to reach the A100/SM80 Nemotron 3 Super NVFP4 Marlin W8A16 compiled path.
Branches:

Failing repro:
https://github.com/mikekg/vllm/tree/pytorch-185862-a100-contiguous-repro
Explicit materialization workaround:
https://github.com/mikekg/vllm/tree/pytorch-185862-a100-contiguous-repro%2Btorch-empty-copy-fix

The public repro base is composed from these vLLM changes:

[Quant][Triton] Support modelopt_mixed on SM80/SM86 (Ampere): vllm-project/vllm#42610
Allow native KV cache dtype in Triton cache update: vllm-project/vllm#43330
Pad FP4 Marlin weights to valid thread tiles: vllm-project/vllm#43806
Pad FP8 Marlin weights to valid thread tiles: vllm-project/vllm#43910
Pad NVFP4 Marlin MoE intermediate tiles: vllm-project/vllm#43908

Repro shape:

Hardware: A100 / SM80, 4 GPUs.
Model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4.
Tokenizer: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16.
Tensor parallel size: 4.
KV cache dtype: FP8.
Dense FP8 linear backend: MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.
Execution: torch.compile enabled, CUDA graph capture enabled.
No eager fallback.
No graph partition around Marlin.

Download the model parser:
curl -O https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16/raw/main/super_v3_reasoning_parser.py
Run vLLM from one of the repro branches and start the server:
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 \
  --tokenizer nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 \
  --served-model-name nvidia/nemotron-3-super \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2560 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --dtype auto \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --async-scheduling \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 128 \
  --moe-backend marlin \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --reasoning-parser-plugin ./super_v3_reasoning_parser.py \
  --reasoning-parser super_v3
Then send this request:
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H '<REDACTED> EMPTY' \
  -d '{
    "model": "nvidia/nemotron-3-super",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "What is the capital of Japan? Answer with just the city name."
      }
    ],
    "max_tokens": 64,
    "temperature": 0.2,
    "top_k": 1,
    "include_reasoning": false,
    "chat_template_kwargs": {
      "enable_thinking": false,
      "thinking": false,
      "force_nonempty_content": true
    }
  }'
Expected outcomes:

pytorch-185862-a100-contiguous-repro: fails in the full serving graph. The observed deterministic failure signature is expected "Tokyo", got " ј".
pytorch-185862-a100-contiguous-repro+torch-empty-copy-fix: passes the same request because the logical Marlin output is explicitly materialized with torch.empty(...) plus copy_() after slicing, instead of relying on .contiguous() alone.

Why I Think This May Be A Compiler Issue
In eager PyTorch, for runtime M > 1, the result of:
x[:, :logical_n].contiguous()
is compact if x has row stride padded_n and padded_n != logical_n.
The larger compiled artifact appears to preserve a layout that is only contiguous for the M == 1 corner case, while the symbolic dimension can be larger than one.
If PyTorch's architectural intent is that .contiguous() should match eager semantics for all guarded runtime values, then this looks like a missing materialization or missing guard in the larger compiled path.
If PyTorch's architectural intent is that .contiguous() may preserve such a layout for symbolic dimensions unless a downstream callee/operator advertises a compact/fixed-stride requirement, then the affected callee/operator in the vLLM MambaMixer2 path should be fixed to advertise or materialize that requirement. I would appreciate guidance on that intended contract.
Workaround Used Locally
The local workaround is to spell out the materialization:
sliced = x[:, :logical_n]
out = torch.empty(
    sliced.shape,
    dtype=sliced.dtype,
    device=sliced.device,
)
out.copy_(sliced)
return out
That produces an explicit copy-slice kernel in the generated artifact and returns a compact (logical_n, 1) row-major stride.
Desired Behavior / Question
I would like guidance on the intended compiler behavior here.
My expected behavior is that torch.compile should preserve the eager semantic effect of .contiguous() for a slice whose contiguity depends on a symbolic dimension. If the dimension is not proven to be one, I would expect the compiled graph to materialize a compact output or guard on the runtime condition that makes the original view contiguous.
If that expectation is not the intended contract for symbolic-shape compiled graphs, please clarify the intended rule. In that case, should every downstream callee/operator that requires compact/fixed-stride layout advertise that requirement? If so, what is the intended mechanism for captured Triton callees/operators as well as dispatcher custom ops?

🐛 Describe the bug
The Im2Col op has a metal kernel that uses 64-bit integers for positions and strides. While this avoids the overflow issues causing corruptions like was investigated for Col2Im in #185664, it also causes similar perf regression for the cases where the 32-bit integers would have been sufficient due to the 64-bit multiplications in the hot path of the kernel.
